chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn Ahmad ibn A'sham from some of our companions from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I heard him say: 'The time for Maghrib is when the redness (of sunset) departs from the east. Do you know how that is?' I said: 'No.' He said: 'Because the east is opposite the west. Like this,' and he raised his right hand above his left. 'When it disappears here, the redness departs from here.'

key_terms.الْحُمْرَةُ: The redness (referring to the red glow of sunset)

ai.seo_question: When does the time for Maghrib prayer begin according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the precise boundary for Maghrib prayer by linking the disappearance of the western sunset's redness to its simultaneous fading in the east, a phenomenon known as *Al-Humrah al-Sharqiyyah*. This definition distinguishes the start of Maghrib time from the end of Asr, which concludes with the disappearance of the redness in the west, thereby establishing a clear chronological sequence for the daily prayers. The Imam’s physical demonstration underscores the geometric relationship between the sun's setting point and the eastern horizon, providing a practical method for determining prayer times before the advent of modern astronomical calculations.
